os_version: Ubuntu 24.04, GTK 4.14, gtk4-widget-factory (spinner + progress bars animating)
channel_setup: gdb tap capturing consecutive GSK render-tree frames; structural diff computed with embedded texture payloads masked.

t1_read_text.detail: Static content decodes as in the text-editor cell.

t4_living_screen.detail: Across 12 consecutive frames of an animating UI (spinner + progress bars), the semantic inter-frame diff is 15-19 changed lines = ~0.9-1.1 KB, isolating exactly the animating widgets. A screenshot policy would pay ~1366 tokens EVERY frame regardless; the structured diff pays only for what moved, and an idle frame diffs to ~0.

measurements.notes: Native mirror of the browser living-screen result: event-shaped diffs ~1 KB/frame on animation vs a flat 1366 tok/frame screenshot cost. Full serialized frame is ~340 KB but 57% of that is embedded texture payloads (stable identity, sent once); the DIFF is what matters for a moving screen and it is tiny. Confirms the frames-vs-diffs economics hold on a native toolkit, not just Chromium.

runtime_verification.method: structural diff of consecutive intercepted trees (textures masked)
runtime_verification.agreement: diffs localize to the animating widgets only
